title: Database changes are only ever tested on an empty database
what: The cloud database check builds a brand-new empty database, applies every database change in order, then runs the tests. There is no starting data, so the part of each change that rewrites or fills in existing rows (about 62 of the 98 change files do this) runs on nothing. Nothing checks that a gym's old members, receipts or workouts come through a change unchanged.
expected: Before a database change goes live, it is tried on a database that already holds realistic old rows (for example the demo gym made by the previous version), and the old rows are checked afterwards.
how_often: every database change that touches existing rows
fix_line: Load a saved demo gym from the previous version before applying the new changes, then compare its rows

title: The watch app's What's new on Google Play repeats the phone's notes
what: When a release goes to Google Play, the watch app is given exactly the same What's new text as the phone app. A watch user reads about phone-only changes, and if the notes are long, a watch line can be cut off to fit Play's limit while phone lines stay.
expected: The watch's What's new on Play lists the watch's own changes, or says plainly that nothing changed on the watch.
fix_line: Mark watch lines in the What's new list and give the watch upload only those

title: No cloud test ever pairs the watch with the phone
what: The cloud phone test has no watch: a stand-in pretends one is there just to photograph the welcome screen. The watch build test checks each side's message reader on its own. Nothing follows a set or weight entered on the watch all the way to the phone's saved workout, the gym's server and Health Connect, so a value lost or changed between them would pass every check.
expected: At least one cloud run pairs a watch emulator with a phone emulator, logs a set on the watch, and checks the same numbers on the phone, the server and Health Connect.
fix_line: Add one paired watch-and-phone run to the release checks
